column1: # Resistance-associated chromosomal loci. NOT a stage: `regulators` is an
# internal step folded into its owning rule by spec.md:351, and is screened
# alongside `amr` (stage 4). Stage 6 is `variants` and is a different thing.
# EDITABLE REFERENCE TABLE - not hard-coded in any analysis script.
# gene            : locus name, must match config/mechanisms.tsv `gene`
# mechanism       : mechanism class assigned on detection
# gene_role       : controlled vocabulary from papipeline.models.GeneRole
# screen_for      : comma-separated variant classes to look for
# promoter_screen : whether promoter-region assessment is in scope
# reference_length : expected locus length in bp, used to sanity-check calls
# evidence_level  : ceiling on the claim from a variant call in this locus
# notes           : caveats
# A variant call in any of these loci is reported as a variant plus its
# mechanism. It is NOT reported as phenotypic resistance. Establishing an
# association requires stage 12; robustness requires stage 13.
# locus_tag       : PAO1 RefSeq tag, resolved and verified by
#                   scripts/resolve_locus_tags.py. Name= matching
#                   fails for mexZ/mexS/dacB: the first has no
#                   such feature and no NCBI alias, so it is
#                   resolved by adjacency to the mexXY pump; the
#                   second has no PAO1 counterpart at all; the
#                   third carries no dacB symbol in PAO1 and is
#                   resolved from the literature. Empty means the
#                   locus is absent from PAO1 - see its notes.

column1: dacB
column9: Cell-wall remodelling context. Causality is not claimed. LOCUS_TAG resolved by scripts/resolve_locus_tags.py (resolved from the literature, verified in the GFF): PA3047 is a single 1431 bp gene feature (3410264-3411694+) GFF carries Dbxref=GeneID:882878 as its own cross-reference dacB is PBP4 in P. aeruginosa. PAO1 has no gene carrying the symbol `dacB` - NCBI Gene has no PAO1 dacB record at all (txid83333 returns E. coli records only), so no search can resolve it. The identity is from the literature, which is where a function-to-gene assignment like this actually lives: papers cloning and studying 'the PA3047 gene... for PBP4 from P. aeruginosa PAO1', and a 2024 enumeration of P. aeruginosa PBPs listing 'PBP4 (dacB, PA3047)'. NOTE: PBP4 and ampC are functionally linked - PBP4 loss derepresses ampC - but they are NOT physically adjacent on the chromosome. An operon-adjacency check does not apply to dacB and must not be used to disqualify it; that heuristic was wrong here and it wrongly suggested PA3047 was not dacB.
